h1: The 7 Best Bissell Upright Vacuums of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: seven Bissell upright vacuums from the dual-brush Pet Hair Eraser to compact CleanView models, by pets, allergies and storage.
summary: The Bissell Pet Hair Eraser 42946 is the best Bissell upright, stacking self-cleaning dual brush rolls, a HEPA sealed system and headlights. The CleanView Swivel Pet 2252 is the better value for shedding pets. The 39883 suits allergy households, and the 3536 and 3508 fit apartments and tight storage.
intro: Bissell uprights read like a wall of near-identical model numbers, and the useful differences hide in three places: the brush system, the filter and how the machine fits in a closet. Shoppers who compare only price end up with a vacuum that fights their pet's coat or exhales fine dust back into a bedroom. A two-digit price gap often buys a different brush, not a better motor.

We ranked seven Bissell uprights from their listings, scoring brush design, filtration, dirt tank capacity, maneuverability and storage footprint. Several listings say very little, so we kept every claim to what the page actually states and flagged thin entries. Where a spec is absent, treat it as unconfirmed, not as a feature the model lacks.

products.name: Bissell Pet Hair Eraser DualBrush Upright Vacuum with Two Brush Rolls, DualBrush Self-Cleaning Technology, HEPA Sealed Allergen System, Bright FurFinder Headlights, Lift-Off Pod, 42946
products.verdict: Bissell's newest dual-brush hardware with HEPA and headlights.
products.description:
The 42946 is Bissell's most complete upright here. It pairs two brush rolls with DualBrush self-cleaning technology, a HEPA sealed allergen system and FurFinder headlights, plus a lift-off pod for stairs and furniture. Self-cleaning brushes matter because hair wrapping the roll is the top reason uprights lose pickup, and the sealed HEPA path keeps fine particles inside the machine.

It leads the 2252 by adding those three features at the $200 to $500 price, a clear step above the $100 to $200 pet model. The headlights are a small touch that pay off on dark floors, where pet hair is easy to miss. No other model in this ranking lists HEPA together with a brush that clears itself.

Buy it for a household with pets and allergies that wants the newest Bissell hardware. It costs the most of the group and has more parts to maintain, so skip it if you want the cheapest upright.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want Bissell's newest hardware.

products.name: Bissell CleanView Swivel Pet Upright Vacuum, Swivel Steering for Maneuverability, Triple Action Brush Roll for Pet Hair, Large Capacity Dirt Tank & Scatter-Free Tech, 2252
products.verdict: Swivel steering and a triple action brush for pet hair.
products.description:
The CleanView Swivel Pet 2252 is the shedding-pet workhorse. Swivel steering helps turns around chair legs, a Triple Action Brush Roll is aimed at pet hair, and the large dirt tank means fewer trips to the bin. Scatter-Free Tech is meant to stop the roll from flicking debris out the front.

It lands second because it undercuts the 42946 at the $100 to $200 level but gives up the dual self-cleaning brushes and the HEPA sealed system. Against the 3836 below, it adds pet-specific wording and the larger tank, which is why the sibling sits lower. For furry floors on a sensible budget, this is the cleanest value in the lineup.

Buy it if shedding is the main problem. Skip it if allergies drive the purchase, because no HEPA system is listed. It also has a single brush roll, so tangled hair still needs manual clearing.

products.name: Bissell Pet Hair Eraser Allergen Lift-Off, HEPA, 39883
products.verdict: A Pet Hair Eraser with HEPA and a lift-off design.
products.description:
The Pet Hair Eraser Allergen Lift-Off 39883 is named for what it filters. HEPA filtration and a lift-off design define the listing, and the Pet Hair Eraser line suggests a pet-hair focus. HEPA matters because standard filters let fine dust and dander pass through, which allergy sufferers feel in the air.

It ranks third because the listing is thin. There is no brush spec and little else beyond the title, so compared with the 42946 and 2252 you are buying on the name. It sits in the $100 to $200 bracket, the same as the 2252, but the 2252 describes its hardware more fully.

Choose it if allergies are your priority and you want HEPA at a mid-range price. Before ordering, confirm the full spec list on the product page. The lack of a stated brush roll or tank size is the real caveat here, not performance.
products.skipIf: You want a full feature list.

products.name: Bissell CleanView Upright Vacuum with Active Extension Wand, XL 2L Dirt Tank Capacity, Powerful Suction & OnePass Technology for Carpets & Hard Floors, 3536
products.verdict: A 2L tank and OnePass for carpets and hard floors.
products.description:
The CleanView 3536 suits smaller homes. It lists an XL 2L dirt tank, an active extension wand and OnePass technology for carpets and hard floors, all under $100. A 2L tank is generous at this price, and the wand reaches stairs, cobwebs and furniture edges without a second tool.

It ranks fourth because it lists no pet brush or HEPA system, which the three models above do. In exchange it costs the $50 to $100 bracket, well below the 2252 and 3836. The 3536 beats the 4438 below on documented features, since the 4438 lists almost none.

Choose it for an apartment or a small house with mixed flooring and no heavy shedding. Skip it if you have pets, because a general-purpose brush will leave hair behind. Allergy sufferers should also pass, as no filter wording is given.
pros: Works on carpet and hard floor

products.name: Bissell CleanView Swivel Vacuum, Triple Action Brush Roll, 3836
products.verdict: Swivel handling with a triple action brush roll.
products.description:
The CleanView Swivel 3836 is a general-purpose cousin of the 2252. It lists a Triple Action Brush Roll and swivel handling, in the $100 to $200 bracket, and little else. The swivel line is what makes it relevant, since it eases turns around furniture.

It places fifth because it lacks the pet-hair wording and larger tank of the 2252 at the same price tier, so you gain nothing by choosing it over its sibling. Its edge over the 4438 and 3508 below is the documented brush roll, which gives it a better chance with rugs and mixed floors.

Choose it if you are comparing within the Swivel line and want to confirm details yourself. Skip it if you have shedding pets and want a product that says so. The thin spec list is the caveat, so read the full page for tank size and filter type before you order.

products.name: Bissell CleanView Upright Vacuum, 4438
products.verdict: A CleanView upright aimed at solid performance for less.
products.description:
The CleanView 4438 is the simplest Bissell upright here. Our data lists no features at all, only that it is a CleanView upright in the $50 to $100 bracket. Its appeal is the price and the brand, not documented hardware.

It ranks sixth because we have fewer facts than for any model above, so it cannot be scored against pet, HEPA or tank claims. The 3536 costs the same bracket and lists a 2L tank and an extension wand, so it wins the budget argument on paper. The 4438 only makes sense if you find a significantly better deal.

Choose it if you want a basic Bissell upright and will read the listing for specifics. Skip it if you need allergen filtering, pet hair performance or a known tank size. The caveat is blunt: you are buying with little information to compare.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a Bissell upright for less.

products.name: Bissell CleanView Compact, Powerful Suction & Extension Wand, 3508
products.verdict: A compact CleanView with an extension wand.
products.description:
The CleanView Compact 3508 is built for tight storage. It lists powerful suction and an extension wand in a compact body, in the $50 to $100 bracket. Compact uprights fit closets and corners where a full-size machine will not, and the wand lets you reach stairs and ledges.

It finishes last because it has the thinnest feature set, with no pet brush, HEPA wording or tank size listed. The 3536 beats it on documentation with a 2L tank, so the 3508 only wins when floor space is the constraint, not capacity.

Choose it for small apartments, dorms or a closet where height and width matter. Skip it for a large home, since limited tank detail suggests frequent emptying. Measure the storage spot first, because the compact name alone does not give dimensions.

whatMatters.detail: A brush roll agitates carpet to lift dirt and hair from the fibers. Dual and triple action designs target pet hair and tangles, and self-cleaning versions reduce wrapping. This is the part that touches the floor most, so it shapes real results. Look for brush wording in the title, such as DualBrush or Triple Action, and see if a brush guard or hair cutter is mentioned.

HEPA filtration captures fine particles that standard filters pass back into the room, which matters most for allergy or asthma sufferers. A sealed system stops leaks around the filter. The 42946 and 39883 list HEPA. Look for the word HEPA or sealed allergen system in the title, and check the filter is washable or replaceable, so upkeep stays cheap.

A bigger dirt tank means fewer trips to the bin, and it matters on large homes or heavy shedding. The 3536 lists an XL 2L tank, and the 2252 lists a large capacity one. Check for a stated liter figure, and be wary of listings that say only large without a number.

Swivel steering makes turns easier around furniture and in cluttered rooms, so you push the vacuum less and steer it more. It matters if your floor plan has many obstacles. The 2252 and 3836 sit in the Swivel line. Look for the word swivel in the title, and confirm the handle pivots freely in a store or from owner photos.

Uprights are tall and awkward to store, so a compact body like the 3508 fits where a full-size model will not. Storage space is a practical limit that specs do not show. Measure your closet height and width, and compare against any listed dimensions before ordering, since many Bissell listings omit them. Leave room to lift the vacuum out without scraping the walls.

faq.q: Which Bissell is best for pet hair?
faq.a: The CleanView Swivel Pet 2252 has a Triple Action Brush Roll aimed at pet hair and a large tank. The 42946 adds dual self-cleaning brushes and HEPA for the cleanest results on shedding coats, at a higher price.

faq.q: What mistake do buyers make with Bissell?
faq.a: Picking by price alone and missing the brush and filter differences. A $50 to $100 model like the 3536 lacks pet and HEPA features that the 2252 and 42946 list. Compare those first, then price.

faq.q: Is the 42946 worth it over the 2252?
faq.a: If you want HEPA and dual self-cleaning brushes, yes. The 2252 costs less and handles pet hair well on paper, but it lists no HEPA system, so allergy households should pay for the 42946.

faq.q: How do I clean the brush roll?
faq.a: Remove the roll and clear hair by hand with scissors. The 42946 lists self-cleaning technology, which reduces wrap, but you should still check the roll every few uses, because string and long hairs can bind the bearings.

faq.q: How do I maintain the filter?
faq.a: Rinse or replace it per the manual, since schedules vary by model. HEPA filters on the 42946 and 39883 matter most to allergy owners, so do not skip it, and rinse a washable one only after it is fully dry.

faq.q: Can a compact upright handle a whole home?
faq.a: The 3508 is compact and best for smaller homes. It lists no tank size, so a larger home may need more frequent emptying. The 3536 with its 2L tank is better for bigger floors, though neither replaces a larger upright in a big house.

finalTake: For most homes with pets, the Bissell Pet Hair Eraser 42946 is the best upright, with self-cleaning dual brushes and a HEPA sealed system. The CleanView Swivel Pet 2252 is the budget-friendly pick for shedding. Choose the 39883 for allergies, the 3536 for an apartment and the 3508 when storage space is tight.
